caseStudy.context: After working on web and desktop projects, I wanted to explore a new universe: mobile. For my first experience with Flutter, I chose a game whose rules fit in a few lines, but where every interaction matters. Tic-Tac-Toe became my playground for learning by building.
caseStudy.role: Mobile design and development with Flutter and Dart, from the interface to the game modes and Minimax opponent.
constraints: Discover Flutter and Dart while building a genuinely playable app
Bring two experiences together: local head-to-head and solo against the computer
Make the active player, starting move and game result easy to read
Give solo mode an opponent that thinks ahead using Minimax
approach: Start with a home screen that makes the choice between head-to-head and solo play immediate
Make the board and turn indicator the thread running through every game
Add a starting-player choice, then bring in Minimax to power the bot
Polish the end-of-game states and rematch so it is easy to jump back in
caseStudy.outcome: The result is more than a grid that fills up: it is a first mobile game with two modes, a complete play-through and a Minimax AI. This tiny arcade marks my entrance into the Flutter universe — a simple format, but a real first step in mobile development.
